crossRefs.note: He came and took her by the hand, and raised her up. The fever left her immediately, and she served them.
Peter sent them all out, and knelt down and prayed. Turning to the body, he said, “Tabitha, get up!” She opened her…
He gave her his hand, and raised her up. Calling the saints and widows, he presented her alive.
Being moved with compassion, he stretched out his hand, and touched him, and said to him, “I want to. Be made clean.”
God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.
For he spoke, and it was done. He commanded, and it stood firm.
He came near and touched the coffin, and the bearers stood still. He said, “Young man, I tell you, arise!”
He who was dead sat up, and began to speak. And he gave him to his mother.
But he put them all outside, and taking her by the hand, he called, saying, “Child, arise!”
Her spirit returned, and she rose up immediately. He commanded that something be given to her to eat.

parallels.note: But he put them all outside, and taking her by the hand, he called, saying, “Child, arise!”

translations.web: Taking the child by the hand, he said to her, “Talitha cumi!” which means, being interpreted, “Girl, I tell you, get up!”
translations.bsb: Taking her by the hand, Jesus said, “Talitha koum!” which means, “Little girl, I say to you, get up!”
translations.kjv: And he took the damsel by the hand, and said unto her, Talitha cumi; which is, being interpreted, Damsel, I say unto thee, arise.
translations.asv: And taking the child by the hand, he saith unto her, Talitha cumi; which is, being interpreted, Damsel, I say unto thee, Arise.
